title.narrative: MFF - Energy Sector Development Investment Program (Facility Concept)

description.narrative: The multi tranche financing facility (MFF1) was approved on 28 November 2008 with a total amount of $570 million. The MFF was initially scheduled for 10 years inclusive of procurement and construction activities. The MFF utilization period was extended from 28 November 2018 to 28 November 2020. The MFF was comprised of five trances. Tranches 1 and 2 were closed on 28 November 2018, tranches 3 and 4 were closed on 28 November 2020, and tranche 5 was closed on 28 May 2020. However, the winding-up period of tranches 3 and 4 was extended till 31 December 2023 to be financially closed. The overall outputs of MFF were achieved. The major output components of MFF were comprised of the first phase of the 500 kV Afghanistan-Turkmenistan transmission line, 220 kV NEPS transmission lines, 220/20 kV substations, and distribution networks in northern, southern, and central Afghanistan. MFF also financed the rehabilitation of Sheberghan Gas Fields and a hydropower plant in Helmand Province. The MFF contributed to financing various feasibility studies, designs, infrastructure improvements and maintenance, human resource development, and institutional reforms. The executing agency (EA) for the power component of the Facility was DABS (the government owed electricity utility) and EA for the Gas Wells Rehabilitation component was the Ministry of Mines and Petroleum (MOMP). DABS was responsible for the overall implementation of the Investment Program as well as for all projects to be financed under the MFF except for the Sheberghan gas fields rehabilitation project for which MOMP was the EA.

Output: Generation capacity from hydro sources and gas wells increased Indicator: 3 MW of additional hydropower generated by 2017 Progress/Status: Achieved. The Gereshk hydropower project was upgraded with additional 3MW and completed on 22 October 2020 and DABS issued a completion certificate. Data Source: CSO publications ICE quarterly report DABS annual report Actual value:

Output: Generation capacity from hydro sources and gas wells increased Indicator: 900,000 cubic meters/day additional gas produced by 2016 Progress/Status: Achieved. 1. The 1st phase of gas wells rehabilitation comprises the rehabilitation of 8-12 gas wells in Sheberghan in northern Afghanistan. The contract was awarded to Turkish Petroleum in August 2012 and 6 wells were fully rehabilitated in October 2014.
2. The 2nd phase of gas wells rehabilitation of two existing gas wells (No. 31 & 37) in the Yatimtaq Gas field of Sherberghan), the contract was awarded to Xinjing Zhengtong Oil and Gas Co. Ltd in August 2016 and mobilized in February 2018, and completed in August 2018.
At the project approval, it was envisaged that 900,000 cubic meters per day of gas will be supplied from ten gas wells from Sheberghan Gas Field by 2016, however, eight out of ten gas wells (Well No. 21, 31, 37, 38, 45, 47, 61 and 69) were successful with the gas supply of 628,854 cubic meters per day which is less than as envisaged. The less achievement is because of (i) overestimation of gas reserves at filed and, (ii) the failure of two gas wells (Well No. 29 and 32) due to a technical issue of tubing corrosion in the depth of 1,600 and 1,700 meters and shutdown with no gas supply. Data Source: CSO publications ICE quarterly report DABS annual report Actual value:

Sustainable and reliable grid connected power supply in north, east and south Afghanistan

North East Power System (NEPS) capable to supply 150 megawatts (MW) in 2009 to 1,000 MW of connected load by 2017 Progress/Status: As of Dec 2023, the 87.5 kms of 500-kV transmission line from Turkmenistan border to Sheberghan under MFF1 Tranche 4 (G0332) was 100% completed and completion certificate was issued on 21 October 2020. The 500/220-kV substation under MFF1 Tranche 5 (G0377) is 100% completed and completion certificate was issued on 4 January 2019.
The associated 500-kV transmission line from Sherberghan to Kabul (Arghandi) of around 544 km and 500 kV substation at Dasht-e-Alwan were financed from MFF-2 Tranche 1 (G0464/G0465) and MFF1 Tranche 5 (G0377) and, North-South Power Transmission Enhancement Project (G0374/G0375). The NEPS capacity would be increased to 1,000 megawatts (MW) upon the completion of all the above projects. The work has been stopped of these projects since mid August 2021 due to change of government. Data Source: ICE quarterly report DABS annual report Actual value:

Reduction in system losses from 50% in 2007 to 30% by 2017 Progress/Status: The system losses were reduced to 35.94% as of December 2020 from 50% in 2007. However, currently, due to change in mid-August 2021, the updated figures are not provided as of 31 December 2023. The target will be achieved by the completion of 500-kV transmission line under North-South Power Transmission Enhancement Project once the operation is resume in Afghanistan. The project is 93% completed as of 31 July 2021. Data Source: ICE quarterly report DABS annual report Actual value:
